[1, 4] This significant growth was primarily driven by its data center division, which posted a record revenue of $10.32 billion, a 171% increase year-over-year. [1] In conjunction with the earnings report, Nvidia's Board of Directors approved an additional $25 billion for its share repurchase program. [4] <5> Nvidia announced three new professional desktop workstation GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture at the SIGGRAPH 2023 conference. The RTX 5000 features 12,800 CUDA cores and 32GB of graphics memory. The RTX 4500 has 7,680 CUDA cores with 24GB of memory, while the more compact RTX 4000 is a single-slot GPU. The RTX 5000 was available for purchase at the time of announcement from partners like PNY and HP, with the RTX 4500 and RTX 4000 scheduled for release in the fall of 2023 through partners including BOXX, Dell, HP, and Lenovo. <6> On August 8, 2023, during his keynote address at the SIGGRAPH 2023 conference, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced an upgraded version of the Grace Hopper Superchip, the GH200. The new GH200 platform is designed for complex generative AI workloads and will be available in various configurations. A dual-chip server configuration boasts 144 Arm Neoverse cores and will offer up to 3.5 times more memory capacity (282GB) and 3 times more bandwidth (10TB/sec) than the current generation. Nvidia announced that systems from leading manufacturers equipped with the new Grace Hopper GH200 are expected to become available in the second quarter of 2024. <7> Nvidia announced a major release of its Omniverse platform at the SIGGRAPH 2023 conference. The update introduces new foundation applications and services aimed at helping developers and industrial enterprises enhance their 3D pipelines using the OpenUSD framework and generative AI. Key enhancements include updates to the Omniverse Kit for modular application building, a new Kit Extension Registry, and developer templates. The release also features connections to Adobe Firefly, expanded spatial computing capabilities with OpenXR support for more headsets, and new partners like Cesium, Move AI, and SideFX Houdini connecting to Omniverse via OpenUSD. Additionally, Nvidia and its partners are releasing new RTX workstations and the L40S GPU, which are optimized for Omniverse workflows. The update improves rendering with a new AI denoiser for real-time 4K path tracing and integrates DLSS 3 technology. Upgraded applications include Omniverse USD Composer and Audio2Face, which now has multilingual support and a new female base model. <8> At SIGGRAPH 2023, Nvidia and Hugging Face announced a major partnership to enhance accessibility to generative AI supercomputing for developers. The collaboration integrates Nvidia's DGX Cloud AI supercomputing directly into the Hugging Face platform, which is utilized by over 15,000 organizations and provides access to more than 250,000 models. This integration is delivered through a new offering called 'Training Cluster as a Service,' designed to give developers one-click access to train and fine-tune large language models (LLMs) and other advanced AI applications. The announcement was made by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during his keynote address and was part of a series of reveals, including the next-generation GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip and the Nvidia AI Workbench, aimed at simplifying and scaling enterprise AI projects. <9> Nvidia, ServiceNow, and Accenture jointly launched 'AI Lighthouse,' a program designed to accelerate the development and adoption of enterprise generative AI capabilities. [2, 4, 8] This initiative combines Nvidia's AI supercomputing and software, including its DGX AI supercomputing and NeMo platform, with ServiceNow's enterprise automation platform and Accenture's AI consulting and transformation services. [2, 4] The goal of the program is to assist a select group of pioneering customers in designing, developing, and implementing new generative AI use cases to transform their business operations. [2, 4] <10> On June 26, 2023, at the Snowflake Summit 2023, NVIDIA and Snowflake announced a partnership to provide businesses with an accelerated path to create custom generative AI applications. [5] The collaboration enables enterprises to use their own proprietary data securely within the Snowflake Data Cloud to build and customize large language models (LLMs). [4, 5] This is achieved by integrating NVIDIA's NeMo platform, a framework for developing LLMs, directly into the Snowflake platform, allowing proprietary information to remain secure and governed. [4, 5] The partnership was highlighted in a fireside chat between the CEOs of both companies at the event. [5]

[1, 2, 3] The alleged illegal shipments, which occurred between October 2022 and July 2025, included the high-powered Nvidia H100 GPU. [1, 2, 3] Prosecutors state that some of the chips were routed through Singapore and Malaysia before reaching their final destination in China. [3] If convicted, Geng and Yang could each face up to 20 years in prison under the Export Control Reform Act. [3] <4> NVIDIA has officially announced that its GeForce GPUs based on the Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta architectures will cease to receive Game Ready driver updates after a final release in October 2025. This change will end support for new features, bug fixes, and performance optimizations for a range of older graphics cards, including the GeForce GTX 900 and GTX 10-series. Following the final update, these GPUs will transition to a legacy support model, receiving only quarterly security updates for three additional years, until October 2028. The company noted that this provides a support lifetime of up to 11 years for some of these products, which is beyond typical industry standards. In a related announcement, NVIDIA stated it will extend Game Ready driver support for all its RTX GPUs on the Windows 10 operating system until October 2026, a year beyond Microsoft's official end-of-support date for the OS. <5> Nvidia issued a press release on July 30, 2025, announcing it will host its conference call to discuss the financial results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026 on Wednesday, August 27, 2025. The second quarter concluded on July 27, 2025. Prior to the call, which is scheduled for 2 p.m. PT, written commentary from CFO Colette Kress will be posted on the company's investor relations website. The subsequent Q&A session will be limited to financial analysts and institutional investors. <6> In late July 2025, Nvidia placed an order with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) for 300,000 H20 AI chips, which are specifically designed to comply with U.S. export restrictions for the Chinese market. This decision was driven by unexpectedly strong demand from Chinese technology giants, including Tencent, Alibaba, and ByteDance, prompting a strategic shift from relying solely on existing inventory. The new order will supplement a reported existing stock of 600,000 to 700,000 H20 chips. The move followed the US government's reversal of a previous ban on the sale of H20 chips to China in April 2025, with licenses for their export beginning to be issued in early August 2025. <7> On July 14, 2025, The Motley Fool speculated that Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang, would make a significant announcement on July 16, 2025, potentially concerning the company's efforts to regain access to the Chinese market. This was followed by multiple reports confirming that Huang was scheduled to hold a media briefing in Beijing on July 16. The speculation was driven by the context of U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips to China and Nvidia's development of compliant chips like the H20 to navigate these rules. While an announcement occurred on July 16, the more significant development unfolded later. On August 9, 2025, it was reported that the U.S. Commerce Department had begun issuing licenses to Nvidia, allowing the export of its H20 chips to China. [3] <9> In a historic milestone, Nvidia's market capitalization surpassed $4 trillion on Wednesday, July 9, 2025, making it the first publicly traded company in the world to achieve this valuation. [3, 4, 6] News of the event was widely reported on the same day as shares rose in early trading. [4, 6] The following day, on Thursday, July 10, 2025, Nvidia became the first company to officially close with a market capitalization above the $4 trillion mark, solidifying its position. [1, 8] <10> On July 3, 2025, NVIDIA announced that 20 new games would be added to its GeForce NOW cloud gaming service throughout July 2025.
